lines.say: Why do some volcanoes explode, while others just ooze? Let's cut one open.
lines.caption: Why do volcanoes explode?
lines.cap: Why do some volcanoes explode, while others just ooze? Let's cut one open.

lines.say: Deep underground, hot rock melts into magma. It's lighter than the rock around it, so it slowly rises.
lines.caption: Magma rises
lines.cap: Deep underground, hot rock melts into magma. It's lighter than the rock around it, so it slowly rises.

lines.say: Magma is full of dissolved gas, like a sealed bottle of soda. The weight of the rock above keeps that gas squeezed in.
lines.caption: Dissolved gas
lines.cap: Magma is full of dissolved gas, like a sealed bottle of soda. The weight of the rock above keeps that gas squeezed in.

lines.say: But as the magma nears the surface, the pressure drops, and the gas turns into bubbles that grow fast.
lines.caption: Bubbles grow
lines.cap: But as the magma nears the surface, the pressure drops, and the gas turns into bubbles that grow fast.

lines.say: Thick, sticky magma traps those bubbles, until it all blasts out at once. Boom!
lines.caption: Boom
lines.cap: Thick, sticky magma traps those bubbles, until it all blasts out at once. Boom!

lines.say: Runny magma lets the gas escape gently, so the lava just flows, at around eight hundred to twelve hundred degrees Celsius.
lines.caption: Lava flows
lines.cap: Runny magma lets the gas escape gently, so the lava just flows, at around 800 to 1,200 °C.
